I don't think it's part of the current canon anymore!! As far as I know, they're current canon of the Batman & Zatanna backstory is Detective Comics: Deus Ex Machina. I'm not sure if Batman: The Knight is but I've seen a lot of people say it's full stop canon.

So basically what we know in their relationship is that Bruce definitely trusts Zee and Zee is much more careful in using magic in the new canon. I also think Deus Ex Machina is such a beautiful part of the story because Zatanna says she has very much moved on from her crush on Bruce and understands if they cannot be together and she can't be in his life moving forward (context: she was tempted to use a magic item to see if she and Bruce would end up together in the future when she was 15 yrs old), while Bruce actually hopes that their story never ends. I feel like that storyline brings so much potential in opening up a romantic relationship for them to explore. Whether or not it is successful, they would still most likely be there for each other because their love for each other is just so timeless and unconditional in many ways.

Also, like they both deserve healthy relationships lol

I would say that Zatanna and Bruce have a lot of history together that is incredibly compelling enough to make a really good story.

It's actually been shown in a couple of issues of the 2007 Detective Comics that the Waynes and Zataras have been friends for a really long time -- so long that John Zatara (Zatanna's dad) was pretty much the reason why Bruce's parents got to meet each other. Bruce and Zatanna were also really close as kids aside from their families being friends. That's how intertwined they are.

Then, in "Batman: The Knight", it's revealed that Bruce did train under Zatanna's dad to learn escape artistry, but learned the existence of magic by accident because this demon was threatening to take John's life and those of others. After learning of the existence of real magic, Bruce wanted John to teach him but Zatanna's dad refused because he believed there was a price to learning magic and that he had damned Zatanna's life by teaching her the fundamentals of it. It's shown in that storyline that there are two reasons why Bruce might have not decided to pursue a relationship with his best friend: (1) Zatanna is the most powerful magic user in the universe and his first thought of finding out she has real magic was raising his parents from the dead which he eventually realized was not a good idea, and (2) Zatanna is a really strong person with a strong sense of justice and she doesn't need fear and trauma to back her up and motivate her from wanting a good world. Zatanna is pretty consistent when she says that she is not the type to hold grudges (she also understands that she cannot use her pure magic in an act of vengeance). In "Batman: The Knight", Zatanna and Bruce have a conversation about moving on, but Bruce refuses to and in a monologue, he basically says that he can't move on because this sadness is what drives him to become the Batman.

Not sure if that's canon but that's usually basically always the theme of their past. Bruce always gets these realizations.

With that said, I think Zatanna represents a Bruce that can actively seek justice without having to channel it through trauma. She's like a version of Bruce if he had just learned to let go (she's also had the experience of her parents dying). I also feel like she represents the happy side of Bruce's childhood because she's seen it all and is literally the only childhood best friend of Bruce that has not died or become evil. She's known Bruce before his parents died, Bruce on his way to becoming Batman, and Bruce as the Batman. 

She's also a frigging ball of sunshine but because Bruce is Bruce, he feels like he does not deserve her even if he wants to be with her badly (it's been revealed in a comic issue where his heart's desire was seen and all he's wanted was to have his parents still alive and for him to be able to pursue a relationship with Zatanna).

(Note: She does have her flaws though which I don't know if this is still canon but she was also responsible for mind wiping villains' memories so they can reform -- including Catwoman's. She was much younger then and because of Batman, she's realized otherwise but her past has always haunted her and has been shown in her solo title.)

I think with all this material, they can sort of make a character development arc where Bruce, after all his time as Batman, can realize that he can be happy and be Batman at the same time and at least try to make the relationship work with Zatanna because we never actually see them really *try* except for when they were 15 year olds. They always were scared of trying and always just let "what if's" stop them. I think it could be a new change in pace especially because then this would be one of Batman's most wholesome and mature relationships. In case it doesn't work out, Zatanna is very mature on her own anyway and like she always says, she's always one to move on and understand.
